# @volcanicminds/tools: reference for AI agents

> Tree-shakeable TypeScript utilities for the Volcanic Minds stack: TOTP MFA, SMTP mailer, logger
> facade, S3/Minio storage, resumable uploads (tus), AI SDK 7 wiring (models, agents, embeddings,
> pgvector store, tools) and an MCP server for the same tools. Version 0.2.x, branch `v5`, paired with
> `@volcanicminds/backend` 5.x. The source in `lib/` is the authority when this file and the code differ.

## Requirements

- Node.js >= 26, ESM only (`"type": "module"`). In TypeScript with `module: NodeNext`, local imports
  carry the `.js` extension.
- `npm install @volcanicminds/tools`
- Regular dependencies (installed with the package): `otpauth`, `qrcode`, `nodemailer`, `minio`,
  `@aws-sdk/client-s3`, `@tus/server`, `@tus/file-store`, `@tus/s3-store`, `@standard-schema/spec`.
- Optional peer dependencies, needed only by `ai` and `mcp` (install them yourself):

| Peer | Needed by | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ai` ^7 | `/ai` | models, agents, embeddings, `toAiTools` |
| `@ai-sdk/openai` ^4 | `/ai` | `provider: 'openai'` |
| `@ai-sdk/anthropic` ^4 | `/ai` | `provider: 'anthropic'` (chat only) |
| `@ai-sdk/google` ^4 | `/ai` | `provider: 'google'` |
| `@ai-sdk/mistral` ^4 | `/ai` | `provider: 'mistral'` |
| `ai-sdk-ollama` ^4 | `/ai` | `provider: 'ollama'` |
| `@ai-sdk/otel` ^1 | `/ai` | OpenTelemetry spans for AI calls (opt-in by installing it) |
| `@modelcontextprotocol/server` ^2 | `/mcp` | `createMcpHandler` |

`ai` 7 itself lists `zod` (^3.25.76 or ^4.1.8) as its peer. Tool input schemas need Zod 4.2 or later (see
"Tools"); the application installs `zod`, this package does not.

## Entry points

| Import | Source | Exports |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@volcanicminds/tools/mfa` | `lib/mfa/index.ts` | `generateSecret`, `generateSetupDetails`, `verifyToken`, `verifyTokenDelta`, `generateToken`, type `MfaSetupDetails` |
| `@volcanicminds/tools/mailer` | `lib/mailer/index.ts` | `Mailer`, types `MailerConfig`, `MailOptions`, `MailAttachment` |
| `@volcanicminds/tools/logger` | `lib/util/logger.ts` | `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, `fatal` |
| `@volcanicminds/tools/storage` | `lib/storage/index.ts` | `StorageManager`, types `StorageConfig`, `UploadOptions`, `UploadedObjectInfo` |
| `@volcanicminds/tools/transfer` | `lib/transfer/index.ts` | `TransferManager`, types `TransferConfig`, `TransferEventCallback`, `TransferValidator`, `TransferRequest`, `AnonymousTransferCheck` |
| `@volcanicminds/tools/ai` | `lib/ai/index.ts` | see "AI module" |
| `@volcanicminds/tools/mcp` | `lib/mcp/index.ts` | see "MCP server" |
| `@volcanicminds/tools` | `index.ts` | namespaces `mfa`, `mailer`, `log`, `storage`, `transfer`, `ai`, `mcp` |

Prefer the subpaths. The root entry re-exports every module as a namespace
(`import { mfa, log } from '@volcanicminds/tools'`), so it loads `nodemailer`, `minio` and the tus packages
even when only one module is used. It does not load the optional peers: `ai`, the provider SDKs,
`@ai-sdk/otel` and `@modelcontextprotocol/server` are imported dynamically on first use.

## Conventions shared by every module

- Configuration is injected as an object (constructor or function argument). Only `/ai` reads
  `process.env`, as an explicit fallback when a config value is missing.
- Modules do not depend on each other, except `/mcp`, which reuses the tool contract of `/ai`
  (`lib/ai/tool.ts`, no runtime imports).
- No module starts a process, a timer or a connection at import time.

---

## MFA (`/mfa`)

TOTP (RFC 6238) on `otpauth`, QR codes on `qrcode`. Fixed parameters: SHA1, 6 digits, 30 second period.
No environment variables.

```typescript
interface MfaSetupDetails {
  secret: string // base32
  uri: string    // the otpauth://totp/ URI
  qrCode: string // PNG data URL (QRCode.toDataURL of the uri)
}

function generateSecret(size?: number): string                       // random base32, size in bytes, default 20
function generateSetupDetails(appName: string, username: string, secret?: string): Promise<MfaSetupDetails>
function verifyTokenDelta(token: string, secret: string, window?: number): number | null
function verifyToken(token: string, secret: string, window?: number): boolean
function generateToken(secret: string): string                       // current code, for tests and tooling
```

- `generateSetupDetails`: `appName` is the issuer, `username` the label; without `secret` a new 20 byte
  secret is generated.
- `verifyTokenDelta` returns the matched time-step offset (0 current, -1 previous, 1 next) or `null`.
  `window` defaults to 1 (one period either side, about +/- 30 s). An empty token or secret returns `null`.
  Use the delta for anti-replay: record the absolute step consumed and refuse the same or an earlier step.
- `verifyToken(token, secret, window)` is `verifyTokenDelta(token, secret, window) !== null`.
- Errors: a secret that is not valid base32 makes `otpauth` throw (from `verify*`, `generateToken` and
  `generateSetupDetails` with an explicit secret).

```typescript
import * as mfa from '@volcanicminds/tools/mfa'

const setup = await mfa.generateSetupDetails('MyApp', 'user@example.com')
// store setup.secret (encrypted), show setup.qrCode to the user
const delta = mfa.verifyTokenDelta('123456', setup.secret)
if (delta === null) throw new Error('Invalid code')
```

## Mailer (`/mailer`)

`nodemailer` SMTP transport with defaults and a plain text fallback. No environment variables.

```typescript
interface MailerConfig {
  host: string
  port: number
  secure?: boolean                 // default: port === 465
  auth?: { user: string; pass: string }
  defaultFrom?: string
  defaultReplyTo?: string
  tls?: { rejectUnauthorized?: boolean; ciphers?: string }
}

interface MailAttachment { filename: string; content?: string | Buffer; path?: string; contentType?: string; cid?: string }

interface MailOptions {
  to: string | string[]
  subject: string
  html: string                     // required
  text?: string                    // default: derived from html
  from?: string                    // default: config.defaultFrom
  cc?: string | string[]
  bcc?: string | string[]
  replyTo?: string                 // default: config.defaultReplyTo
  attachments?: MailAttachment[]
}

class Mailer {
  constructor(config: MailerConfig)
  send(options: MailOptions): Promise<unknown>   // nodemailer's info object, typed unknown
  verifyConnection(): Promise<boolean>
}
```

- Arrays in `to`, `cc`, `bcc` are joined with `, `.
- Text fallback: `<br>` becomes a newline, `</p>` two newlines, every other tag is stripped, then trimmed.
  It does not decode HTML entities and does not sanitize `html`: escape any user data you interpolate.
- Errors: `send` throws `Error('Email "from" address is required (either in options or config.defaultFrom)')`
  when neither is set, and wraps a transport failure as `Error('Failed to send email to <to>: <message>')`
  (the original error is not attached as `cause`). `verifyConnection` never throws: it logs with
  `console.error` and returns `false`.
- The return value is `unknown`: cast it (`as { messageId?: string }`) before reading fields.

```typescript
import { Mailer } from '@volcanicminds/tools/mailer'

const mailer = new Mailer({
  host: 'smtp.example.com',
  port: 587,
  auth: { user: 'smtp-user', pass: 'smtp-password' },
  defaultFrom: '"My Service" <noreply@example.com>'
})
if (!(await mailer.verifyConnection())) throw new Error('SMTP not reachable')
const info = (await mailer.send({ to: 'user@example.com', subject: 'Hello', html: '<p>Hi</p>' })) as { messageId?: string }
```

## Logger (`/logger`)

A facade over a Pino-like logger the host process puts on the globals. Each function is
`(data: unknown, ...args: unknown[]) => void`: `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, `fatal`.

- It writes only when `globalThis.isLoggingEnabled` is truthy and `globalThis.log` has the method;
  otherwise it does nothing and never throws.
- `@volcanicminds/backend` 5 sets `global.log` but never sets `global.isLoggingEnabled`: inside a backend
  application these calls are silent until the application sets `global.isLoggingEnabled = true`.

```typescript
import * as log from '@volcanicminds/tools/logger'

// once, if the host does not set it; the package ships no global type for this flag
;(globalThis as { isLoggingEnabled?: boolean }).isLoggingEnabled = true
log.info('Application started')
log.error({ err: new Error('Oops') }, 'Something went wrong')
```

## Storage (`/storage`)

S3 compatible object storage on the `minio` client, bound to one bucket. No environment variables.

```typescript
interface StorageConfig {
  endPoint: string        // host name, no scheme
  port: number
  useSSL: boolean
  accessKey: string
  secretKey: string
  bucket: string
  region?: string         // default 'us-east-1'
  pathStyle?: boolean
}
interface UploadOptions { size?: number; contentType?: string; metadata?: Record<string, string | number | boolean> }
interface UploadedObjectInfo { etag: string; versionId: string | null }

class StorageManager {
  constructor(config: StorageConfig)
  getClient(): Client                     // the underlying minio Client
  getBucketName(): string
  verifyConnection(): Promise<boolean>    // listBuckets; logs with console.error and returns false on failure
  ensureBucket(bucketName?: string): Promise<void>   // creates it in `region` if missing
  uploadFile(objectName: string, stream: Readable | Buffer | string, options?: UploadOptions): Promise<UploadedObjectInfo>
  getFileUrl(objectName: string, expiry?: number): Promise<string>    // presigned GET, seconds, default 86400
  getUploadUrl(objectName: string, expiry?: number): Promise<string>  // presigned PUT, seconds, default 86400
  deleteFile(objectName: string): Promise<void>
  deleteFiles(objectNames: string[]): Promise<void>
  fileExists(objectName: string): Promise<boolean>
  getFileStream(objectName: string): Promise<Readable>
  getFileStat(objectName: string): Promise<BucketItemStat>          // minio's stat object
}
```

- Object names are validated: empty, containing `..` or `\`, or starting with `/` or `./` throws
  `Error('Invalid object name: <name>')` (or `'Object name cannot be empty'`). `deleteFiles` validates every name first.
- `uploadFile` calls `ensureBucket()` on every upload. A `string` body is uploaded as content, not read as a
  file path. `options.size` and `options.metadata` reach `putObject`; `options.contentType` is currently
  ignored: to set the content type, put `'Content-Type'` in `metadata`.
- `ensureBucket` wraps failures as `Error('Failed to ensure bucket <name>: <error>')`.
- `fileExists` returns `false` only for minio's `NotFound`; any other error is rethrown.

```typescript
import { StorageManager } from '@volcanicminds/tools/storage'

const storage = new StorageManager({
  endPoint: 'minio.example.com', port: 9000, useSSL: true,
  accessKey: 'access-key', secretKey: 'secret-key', bucket: 'my-bucket'
})
await storage.uploadFile('avatars/42.png', pngBuffer, { metadata: { 'Content-Type': 'image/png' } })
const url = await storage.getFileUrl('avatars/42.png', 3600)
```

## Transfer (`/transfer`)

Resumable uploads (tus protocol) on `@tus/server` 2, stored on the local disk (`@tus/file-store`) or on S3/Minio
(`@tus/s3-store`). No environment variables.

```typescript
interface TransferConfig {
  driver: 'local' | 's3'
  path: string                         // URL path the endpoint answers on, e.g. '/files'
  maxSize?: number                     // bytes; default unlimited
  local?: { directory: string }        // required with driver 'local'
  s3?: {                               // required with driver 's3'
    bucket: string
    endPoint: string                   // host name, no scheme
    port?: number
    useSSL?: boolean                   // default false (http)
    accessKey: string
    secretKey: string
    region?: string                    // default 'us-east-1'
    partSize?: number                  // bytes, default 8 MiB; S3 minimum is 5 MiB
  }
}

type TransferEventCallback = (uploadOrId: Upload | string, req?: IncomingMessage, res?: ServerResponse) => void
type TransferValidator = (req: IncomingMessage, res: ServerResponse) => Promise<void>
type TransferRequest = Pick<IncomingMessage, 'headers' | 'method' | 'url'>
type AnonymousTransferCheck = (req: TransferRequest) => boolean | Promise<boolean>

class TransferManager {
  constructor(config: TransferConfig)
  isImplemented(): boolean                          // always true
  getPath(): string                                 // config.path
  getServer(): Server                               // the @tus/server instance
  handle(req: IncomingMessage, res: ServerResponse): Promise<void>  // Node request handler
  setValidator(validator: TransferValidator): void
  setAnonymousAccess(check: AnonymousTransferCheck): void
  isValid(req: TransferRequest): Promise<boolean>
  onUploadCreate(callback: TransferEventCallback): void     // callback(upload, req)
  onUploadFinish(callback: TransferEventCallback): void     // callback(upload, req, res)
  onUploadTerminate(callback: TransferEventCallback): void  // callback(uploadId: string, req, res)
}
```

- Construction throws `TransferManager: Local driver requires "directory" path`,
  `TransferManager: S3 driver requires s3 config object` or `TransferManager: Unsupported driver <x>`.
- The S3 store uses path-style addressing and the endpoint `http(s)://endPoint[:port]`.
- The tus server is created with `respectForwardedHeaders: true`: upload URLs are built from
  `X-Forwarded-Host` and `X-Forwarded-Proto`, so put it behind a proxy that sets or strips them.
- `setValidator` runs on every request tus handles (`onIncomingRequest`). A validator that throws refuses
  the request: tus answers with the error's `status_code` and `body` when present, otherwise 500.
- `isValid` returns `true` only when a check set with `setAnonymousAccess` answers exactly `true`;
  without a check it returns `false`.
- Runtime shapes: `@tus/server` 2 converts the Node request to a web `Request` (srvx) before calling hooks.
  Whatever the declared types say, the validator receives `(request: Request, uploadId: string)`, and the
  event callbacks receive that `Request` and a web `Response`: read headers with `req.headers.get('name')`.
  The `Upload` type is `@tus/server`'s; this package does not re-export it.

```typescript
import { TransferManager } from '@volcanicminds/tools/transfer'
import * as log from '@volcanicminds/tools/logger'

const transfer = new TransferManager({ driver: 'local', path: '/files', local: { directory: './uploads' } })
transfer.onUploadFinish((upload) => {
  if (typeof upload !== 'string') log.info({ id: upload.id, size: upload.size }, 'upload finished')
})
```

Without `@volcanicminds/backend`, mount it on any Node or Fastify server. In Fastify 5 call
`reply.hijack()` after `handle`, and register a content type parser that leaves the body unread, because
tus streams it itself:

```typescript
import type { FastifyReply, FastifyRequest } from 'fastify'

async function handler(req: FastifyRequest, reply: FastifyReply) {
  await transfer.handle(req.raw, reply.raw)
  reply.hijack() // tus has already written the response
}
await fastify.register(async (instance) => {
  instance.addContentTypeParser('*', (_req, _payload, done) => done(null))
  instance.all('/files', handler)
  instance.all('/files/*', handler)
})
```

---

## AI module (`/ai`)

Wiring of the AI SDK 7 (`ai`). Every function is async because the SDKs are imported on demand.

### Exports

| Name | Kind | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createModel` | function | `LanguageModel` from config or env |
| `createAgent` | function | the SDK's `ToolLoopAgent`, configured |
| `ConcurrencyGuard`, `ConcurrencyQueueError` | classes | per-provider concurrency limits |
| `createEmbedder`, `embedText`, `embedTexts` | functions | embeddings |
| `PgVectorStore` | class | pgvector table helper |
| `defineTool`, `ToolError`, `ToolCallError`, `isToolError` | function, classes, guard | tool contract |
| `toAiTools`, `callerContext` | functions | tools as an AI SDK tool set, per-call caller |
| `ApiCaller`, `ApiMethod`, `ApiRequest`, `ApiResponse`, `ToolContext`, `ToolDefinition`, `ToolInputSchema` | types | tool contract |
| `AiTools`, `AiCallerContext`, `CallerContext` | types | tool set typing |
| `ModelConfig`, `AgentConfig`, `ProviderName`, `ConcurrencyConfig`, `EmbedderConfig`, `VectorDistance`, `VectorStoreConfig`, `VectorMatch` | types | configs |

`CallerAgentConfig` and `NoTools` (in `lib/ai/types.ts`) are used by `createAgent`'s overloads but are not
exported from `/ai`.

### Providers and environment

```typescript
type ProviderName = 'openai' | 'mistral' | 'ollama' | 'google' | 'anthropic'
interface ModelConfig { provider: ProviderName; model: string; apiKey?: string; baseUrl?: string }
```

Resolution order for each value: config, then the variable below. The key read here is passed explicitly to
the provider SDK's `create*` factory (`createOpenAI`, `createAnthropic`, `createGoogleGenerativeAI`,
`createMistral`, `createOllama`), so the SDKs' own default instances and their env lookups are never used.

| Variable | Used by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AI_PROVIDER` | `createModel`, `createEmbedder` | provider when the config has none |
| `AI_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER` | `createEmbedder` | embedding provider, falls back to `AI_PROVIDER` |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `MISTRAL_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | both | API key per provider |
| `OPENAI_MODEL`, `MISTRAL_MODEL`, `GOOGLE_MODEL`, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, `OLLAMA_MODEL` | `createModel` | chat model id |
| `OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL`, `MISTRAL_EMBEDDING_MODEL`, `GOOGLE_EMBEDDING_MODEL`, `OLLAMA_EMBEDDING_MODEL` | `createEmbedder` | embedding model id |
| `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` | both | Ollama URL (no key needed); `ai-sdk-ollama` defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:11434` |
| `AI_TELEMETRY` | all | `false` disables the telemetry registration |
| `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT` | all | `true` records prompts, responses, tool arguments and embedded texts in spans |

`baseUrl` is passed as `baseURL` to every provider (custom endpoints, proxies).

### `createModel`

```typescript
function createModel(config?: ModelConfig): Promise<LanguageModel>
```

Errors: `AI_PROVIDER is not set and no config provided`, `Unsupported AI Provider: <x>`,
`Model name is required for provider <x>`, `Missing API Key for <x>` (every provider except `ollama`), and
`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` if the provider SDK is not installed.

```typescript
import { createModel } from '@volcanicminds/tools/ai'

const fromEnv = await createModel() // AI_PROVIDER + <PROVIDER>_MODEL + <PROVIDER>_API_KEY
const explicit = await createModel({ provider: 'openai', model: 'your-model-id', apiKey: process.env.MY_KEY })
```

### `createAgent`

```typescript
type AgentConfig<CALL_OPTIONS = never, TOOLS extends ToolSet = {}> =
  Omit<ToolLoopAgentSettings<CALL_OPTIONS, TOOLS>, 'id' | 'model'> & { name: string; model: LanguageModel | ModelConfig }

// overload 1: tools from defineTool (an array)
function createAgent<const DEFS extends readonly ToolDefinition[]>(config: CallerAgentConfig<DEFS>): Promise<ToolLoopAgent<CallerContext, AiTools<DEFS>>>
// overload 2: SDK tools (a record) or no tools
function createAgent<CALL_OPTIONS = never, TOOLS extends ToolSet = {}>(config: AgentConfig<CALL_OPTIONS, TOOLS>): Promise<ToolLoopAgent<CALL_OPTIONS, TOOLS>>
```

- Returns the SDK's `ToolLoopAgent` unchanged in type and behavior. `name` becomes the agent `id` and the
  default `telemetry.functionId` (a `telemetry` you pass is merged over it). `model` may be a
  `LanguageModel` or a `ModelConfig` (resolved with `createModel`). Every other key is the SDK's
  (for example `instructions`, `tools`, `stopWhen`, `prepareStep`, `telemetry`).
- With `tools` as an array of `defineTool` definitions, `createAgent` builds the tool set itself and writes
  `prepareCall`; it throws `Agent '<name>': prepareCall, callOptionsSchema, toolsContext carry the caller of
  tools from defineTool, so createAgent writes them` if the config sets any of those. Each call must pass
  `options: { caller }`; a call without it does not type-check and throws
  `Agent '<name>': no caller, pass options: { caller } with the call` before the model runs.
- Tools from `defineTool` (array) and SDK tools (record) cannot be mixed in one agent.

```typescript
import { tool } from 'ai'
import { z } from 'zod'
import { createAgent } from '@volcanicminds/tools/ai'

const auditor = await createAgent({
  name: 'auditor',
  model: { provider: 'openai', model: 'your-model-id' },
  instructions: 'You are an auditor.',
  tools: {
    invoice: tool({
      description: 'An invoice by number',
      inputSchema: z.object({ number: z.string() }),
      execute: async ({ number }) => ({ number, total: 100 })
    })
  }
})
const { text } = await auditor.generate({ prompt: 'Check invoice 42' })
```

### `ConcurrencyGuard`

```typescript
interface ConcurrencyConfig { [provider: string]: number }
class ConcurrencyGuard {
  constructor(customLimits?: ConcurrencyConfig)   // merged over the defaults
  acquire(provider: string): Promise<void>        // waits in a FIFO queue when the limit is reached
  release(provider: string): void                 // call in finally; unknown provider is a no-op
  run<T>(provider: string, task: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>  // acquire, task, release
}
class ConcurrencyQueueError extends Error {}     // name 'ConcurrencyQueueError'
```

- Defaults: `openai` 5, `mistral` 10, `google` 10, `anthropic` 5, `ollama` 2; any other provider name 2.
  Provider names are lower-cased. A limit of `0` falls back to 2.
- Each provider queue holds at most 100 waiters; the 101st `acquire` throws
  `ConcurrencyQueueError('Queue size limit of 100 reached')`.
- The guard is in-process only and is not applied automatically by `createModel` or `createAgent`: wrap
  the calls yourself, sharing one guard instance.

```typescript
import { ConcurrencyGuard } from '@volcanicminds/tools/ai'

const guard = new ConcurrencyGuard({ ollama: 1 })
const result = await guard.run('openai', () => auditor.generate({ prompt: 'Check invoice 42' }))
```

### Telemetry

- The first call of `createModel`, `createAgent`, `createEmbedder`, `embedText` or `embedTexts` registers
  the AI SDK's OpenTelemetry integration (`new OpenTelemetry({ embedding: true })` from `@ai-sdk/otel`),
  once per process, when `@ai-sdk/otel` is installed and `AI_TELEMETRY` is not `false`. If the package is
  missing nothing happens; any other import error is thrown.
- If an `OpenTelemetry` integration is already registered (`globalThis.AI_SDK_TELEMETRY_INTEGRATIONS`), none
  is added.
- Content (prompts, instructions, responses, tool arguments and results, embedded texts) stays out of spans
  unless `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT=true`. A call's or agent's own
  `telemetry.recordInputs` or `recordOutputs` wins over that default.
- The registry is process-wide: after registration every AI SDK call in the process is traced with the same
  content default, including direct `generateText` or `embed` calls. Calls made before it are not.
- Spans go to the tracer provider already running (with `@volcanicminds/backend`, the one `preload()` starts
  from the `OTEL_*` variables).
- `@ai-sdk/otel` depends on an exact `ai` version; a different `ai` 7 release in the application means two
  copies of `ai` in `node_modules`. It still works because the registry lives on `globalThis`.

```typescript
const agent = await createAgent({ name: 'auditor', model, telemetry: { recordInputs: true } })
```

### Embeddings

```typescript
interface EmbedderConfig { provider?: ProviderName; model?: string; apiKey?: string; baseUrl?: string }

function createEmbedder(config?: EmbedderConfig): Promise<EmbeddingModel>
function embedText(text: string, modelOrConfig?: EmbeddingModel | EmbedderConfig): Promise<number[]>
function embedTexts(texts: string[], modelOrConfig?: EmbeddingModel | EmbedderConfig): Promise<number[][]>
```

- Providers: `openai`, `mistral`, `google`, `ollama`. `anthropic` throws
  `Anthropic does not provide an embeddings API; use openai, mistral, google or ollama`.
- Other errors: `AI_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER/AI_PROVIDER is not set and no config provided`,
  `Unsupported AI Provider: <x>`, `Embedding model name is required for provider <x>`, `Missing API Key for <x>`.
- `embedText` and `embedTexts` accept a ready model (an object with a string `modelId`) or a config; they
  call the SDK's `embed` and `embedMany`. Pass a model created once to avoid re-resolving it per call.

```typescript
import { createEmbedder, embedText, embedTexts } from '@volcanicminds/tools/ai'

const embedder = await createEmbedder({ provider: 'openai', model: 'your-embedding-model' })
const vector = await embedText('hello world', embedder)
const vectors = await embedTexts(['a', 'b'], embedder)
```

### `PgVectorStore`

pgvector helper over any executor with the shape `(sql, params) => Promise<rows[] | { rows }>`: a
node-postgres pool, a PGlite instance, or the `raw.query` of a `@volcanicminds/backend` 5 data handle.

```typescript
type VectorDistance = 'l2' | 'cosine' | 'ip'      // operators <->, <=>, <#> (negative inner product)
interface VectorStoreConfig {
  query: (sql: string, params?: unknown[]) => Promise<any>
  table?: string              // default 'embeddings'
  dimensions: number          // must match the embedding model
  distance?: VectorDistance   // default 'cosine'
  schema?: string             // optional schema qualifier
}
interface VectorMatch { id: string; content: string; metadata: Record<string, unknown> | null; distance: number }

class PgVectorStore {
  constructor(config: VectorStoreConfig)
  init(): Promise<void>       // CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector; CREATE SCHEMA (if schema); CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS
  upsert(id: string, content: string, embedding: number[], metadata?: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<void>
  upsertMany(rows: Array<{ id: string; content: string; embedding: number[]; metadata?: Record<string, unknown> }>): Promise<void>
  search(embedding: number[], k?: number): Promise<VectorMatch[]>   // k default 5, nearest first
  delete(id: string): Promise<void>
  count(): Promise<number>
}
```

- Table: `id text PRIMARY KEY, content text NOT NULL, metadata jsonb, embedding vector(<dimensions>) NOT NULL`.
  No index is created; add an HNSW or IVFFlat index yourself for large tables.
- `upsert` is `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE`; `upsertMany` runs one statement per row, not in a
  transaction.
- Errors: the constructor throws without `query` or with `dimensions < 1`; `upsert` and `search` throw
  `PgVectorStore: embedding length <n> does not match configured dimensions <d>`; SQL errors propagate.
- `table` and `schema` are interpolated as double-quoted identifiers without escaping: pass trusted
  constants only, never request input.
- `vector(n)` and `::vector` are written unqualified, so the `vector` type must resolve through the
  connection's `search_path`.
- The database needs the pgvector extension available. `@volcanicminds/backend` 5 opens PGlite without
  extensions, so its embedded engine cannot run `init()`; use a Postgres server with pgvector, or a PGlite
  you create with `extensions: { vector }` from `@electric-sql/pglite-pgvector`.

```typescript
import { PGlite } from '@electric-sql/pglite'
import { vector } from '@electric-sql/pglite-pgvector'
import { PgVectorStore, embedText } from '@volcanicminds/tools/ai'

const pg = await PGlite.create({ extensions: { vector } })
const store = new PgVectorStore({ query: (sql, params) => pg.query(sql, params), table: 'documents', dimensions: 1536 })
await store.init()
await store.upsert('doc-1', 'the text', await embedText('the text'), { source: 'docs' })
const matches = await store.search(await embedText('a query'), 5)
```

### Tools (`defineTool`, `toAiTools`, `callerContext`)

A tool is defined once and served by two adapters: `toAiTools` (AI SDK) and `createMcpHandler` (`/mcp`).
A tool reaches the application only through `context.call`, an API caller bound to the end user's
credential, so it sees what that person would see.

```typescript
type ToolInputSchema<INPUT = unknown> = StandardSchemaV1<unknown, INPUT> & StandardJSONSchemaV1<unknown, INPUT>
type ApiMethod = 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'PATCH' | 'DELETE'
interface ApiRequest { method: ApiMethod; path: string; query?: Record<string, string>; body?: unknown }
interface ApiResponse { status: number; body: unknown }
type ApiCaller = (request: ApiRequest) => Promise<ApiResponse>
interface ToolContext { call: <T = unknown>(request: ApiRequest) => Promise<T> }
interface ToolDefinition<NAME extends string = string, INPUT = unknown, OUTPUT = unknown> {
  readonly name: NAME
  readonly description: string
  readonly input: ToolInputSchema<INPUT>
  execute(input: INPUT, context: ToolContext): Promise<OUTPUT>
}

function defineTool<const NAME extends string, SCHEMA extends ToolInputSchema, OUTPUT>(definition: {
  name: NAME; description: string; input: SCHEMA
  execute: (input: StandardSchemaV1.InferOutput<SCHEMA>, context: ToolContext) => Promise<OUTPUT>
}): ToolDefinition<NAME, StandardSchemaV1.InferOutput<SCHEMA>, OUTPUT>   // frozen

class ToolError extends Error { constructor(message: string, options?: ErrorOptions) }
class ToolCallError extends ToolError { readonly status: number; readonly code: string | undefined; constructor(response: ApiResponse) }
function isToolError(error: unknown): error is ToolError

type CallerContext = { caller: ApiCaller }
function toAiTools<const DEFS extends readonly ToolDefinition[]>(definitions: DEFS): AiTools<DEFS>
function callerContext<const DEFS extends readonly ToolDefinition[]>(definitions: DEFS, caller: ApiCaller): AiCallerContext<DEFS>
```

- `input` must be Standard Schema and Standard JSON Schema at once: Zod 4.2 or later qualifies, Zod 3 does
  not.
- `defineTool` throws when `name` does not match `/^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$/` or `description` is blank.
  `toAiTools` and `createMcpHandler` throw `Tool '<name>' is defined twice` on duplicate names.
- `call` accepts an API path only. A path that does not start with `/` or that resolves to another origin
  (`//host`, `/\host`) throws a `ToolError` before the caller runs. A 2xx resolves with `body`; any other
  status throws `ToolCallError`, whose message is `<code>: <message>` from the response body (or
  `HTTP <status>`), with `status` and `code` set.
- Error exposure: a `ToolError` (including `ToolCallError`) reaches the model or the MCP client with its
  message. Any other thrown error becomes `ToolError("Tool '<name>' failed")` with the original as `cause`.
- `isToolError` checks a `Symbol.for('volcanicminds.tools.ToolError')` brand, so it works across two copies
  of the package; prefer it to `instanceof`.
- `toAiTools` builds the tool set once (it holds no identity). Each `generateText` or `streamText` call passes
  `toolsContext: callerContext(tools, caller)`. A call without it does not type-check, and at runtime the
  SDK rejects the context (`No caller: pass callerContext(tools, caller) as the toolsContext of the call`)
  before any tool runs.

```typescript
import { generateText } from 'ai'
import { z } from 'zod'
import { defineTool, toAiTools, callerContext, ToolError, type ApiCaller } from '@volcanicminds/tools/ai'

const listVehicles = defineTool({
  name: 'list_vehicles',
  description: 'Vehicles on sale, newest first',
  input: z.object({ brand: z.string().optional() }),
  execute: async (input, { call }) => {
    if (input.brand === '') throw new ToolError('brand cannot be empty')
    return call({ method: 'GET', path: '/vehicles', query: input.brand ? { brand: input.brand } : {} })
  }
})
const tools = [listVehicles] as const
const aiTools = toAiTools(tools) // once, at startup

// per request: `caller` acts as the authenticated user (see the backend section)
const { text } = await generateText({ model, tools: aiTools, toolsContext: callerContext(tools, caller), prompt })

// the same tools in an agent, built once, caller per call
const sales = await createAgent({ name: 'sales', model, instructions: 'Answer about the stock.', tools })
const answer = await sales.generate({ prompt, options: { caller } })
```

---

## MCP server (`/mcp`)

A stateless MCP server over Streamable HTTP, built on `createMcpHandler` of `@modelcontextprotocol/server` 2,
serving tools from `defineTool`. Install `@modelcontextprotocol/server`; `ai` is not needed.

Exports: `createMcpHandler`; types `McpHandlerConfig`, `McpRequestOptions`, `McpHandler`; re-exported from
the tool contract: `defineTool`, `ToolError`, `ToolCallError`, `isToolError`, types `ApiCaller`, `ApiMethod`,
`ApiRequest`, `ApiResponse`, `ToolContext`, `ToolDefinition`, `ToolInputSchema`.

```typescript
interface McpHandlerConfig {
  name: string                          // announced to the client
  version: string
  tools: readonly ToolDefinition[]
  allowedOrigins: readonly string[]     // exact browser origins, required
  onError?: (error: unknown, tool: string) => void
}
interface McpRequestOptions { caller: ApiCaller; parsedBody?: unknown }
interface McpHandler {
  fetch(request: Request, options: McpRequestOptions): Promise<Response>
  close(): Promise<void>
}
function createMcpHandler(config: McpHandlerConfig): Promise<McpHandler>
```

- Web standard: the application converts its request to a `Request` (method, absolute URL, headers) and
  sends back the `Response`. Pass a body the framework already parsed as `parsedBody`. Fastify 5
  `reply.send()` accepts a web `Response` as it is.
- No authentication inside: mount it on an authenticated route of your own and pass, per request, the
  `caller` for that user. The caller reaches the tools through `AsyncLocalStorage`.
- Origin check (DNS rebinding defense): a request whose `Origin` header is not in `allowedOrigins` gets
  403 with a JSON-RPC error body (`code -32000`, `Origin not allowed`) before any tool runs; a request
  without `Origin` (a non-browser client) passes; `[]` admits no browser.
- `allowedOrigins` entries must be exact origins (`scheme://host[:port]`): `*`, a path, a trailing slash or
  `null` make `createMcpHandler` throw `allowedOrigins: '<entry>' is not an origin, write it as scheme://host[:port]`.
- Tool results are returned as one text content item (strings as they are, anything else
  `JSON.stringify`). A failing tool returns `isError: true` with the `ToolError` message; `onError` receives
  the error's `cause` when it has one, which is always the case when the tool threw something other than a
  `ToolError` (the original error).
- Duplicate tool names throw at creation.

```typescript
import { createMcpHandler } from '@volcanicminds/tools/mcp'

const mcp = await createMcpHandler({
  name: 'sales',
  version: '1.0.0',
  tools,
  allowedOrigins: ['https://console.example.com'],
  onError: (error, tool) => log.error({ error, tool }, 'tool failed')
})
// inside your authenticated route
const response = await mcp.fetch(request, { caller, parsedBody: req.body })
```

---

## With `@volcanicminds/backend` 5

The backend imports nothing from this package. The application builds managers on top of it and injects
them into `startServer()` (contracts in the backend's `types/global.d.ts`).

```typescript
import { preload, start as startServer } from '@volcanicminds/backend'
import { start as startDataLayer } from '@volcanicminds/backend/db'
import * as mfa from '@volcanicminds/tools/mfa'
import { Mailer } from '@volcanicminds/tools/mailer'
import { TransferManager } from '@volcanicminds/tools/transfer'

await preload()
const layer = await startDataLayer()

// MfaManagement: generateSetup + verify returning the time-step delta (the backend uses it against replays)
const mfaManager = {
  isImplemented: () => true,
  generateSetup: (appName: string, email: string) => mfa.generateSetupDetails(appName, email),
  verify: (token: string, secret: string) => mfa.verifyTokenDelta(token, secret)
}

// ChallengeDeliveryManagement: the backend hands over data (code, purpose, locale), the app writes the message
const mailer = new Mailer({ host: 'smtp.example.com', port: 587, defaultFrom: 'noreply@example.com' })
const challengeDeliveryManager = {
  isImplemented: () => true,
  deliver: async ({ to, code }: { to: string; code: string }) => {
    await mailer.send({ to, subject: 'Your sign-in code', html: `<p>${code}</p>` })
  }
}

// TransferManagement: TransferManager implements it as it is; the backend mounts it at getPath()
const transferManager = new TransferManager({ driver: 'local', path: '/files', local: { directory: './uploads' } })

await startServer({ ...layer, mfaManager, challengeDeliveryManager, transferManager })
```

- Transfer: the backend mounts the tus endpoint at `getPath()` with its own content type parser and
  `reply.hijack()`. Requests with a valid credential are served; a request with no or an invalid credential
  gets 401 `UNAUTHORIZED` unless `transferManager.isValid(req)` (your `setAnonymousAccess` check, which
  receives the Fastify request) answers `true`, the way to accept signed upload links. Which authenticated
  subject may upload what is the application's decision. The tus validator and hooks receive the web
  `Request` that `@tus/server` builds from the raw Node request, not the Fastify request, so `req.user` is
  not on it.
- Challenge delivery: for login codes (`purpose` `identify` or `verify`) the backend calls `deliver` after
  the response and does not await it (so mail latency does not reveal whether an account exists); a failure
  becomes a log line. For a tenant destruction code (`purpose: 'destruction'`) it awaits `deliver`, and a
  failure answers 503 `DESTRUCTION_FACTOR_NOT_AVAILABLE`. The full message type is
  `ChallengeDelivery` (`channel`, `to`, `code`, `purpose`, `expiresAt`, `plane`, `tenantId`, `subjectId`, `locale`).
- Logger: the backend sets `global.log` but not `global.isLoggingEnabled`; set it to `true` if you want
  `@volcanicminds/tools/logger` to write.
- Vector store on the backend's data layer: use the handle's raw SQL, which runs inside the tenant's
  container (`access` from `@volcanicminds/backend/db`, `dataContext` from `@volcanicminds/backend`):
  `new PgVectorStore({ query: (sql, params) => access(dataContext(req)).raw.query(sql, params), dimensions: 1536 })`.
  On a tenant handle with the `schema` strategy each statement runs with `SET LOCAL search_path` set to the
  tenant schema only, so the `vector` type must be resolvable from there (see `PgVectorStore`). Create the
  table and the extension in a migration or at startup, not per request.
- Tools and MCP: the backend knows nothing about MCP or agents. A caller that acts as the request's user can
  replay the request's own credential through `server.inject` (cookie in `COOKIE` mode, `authorization`
  in `BEARER` mode):

```typescript
import type { ApiCaller } from '@volcanicminds/tools/ai'

const callerFor = (req: FastifyRequest): ApiCaller => async ({ method, path, query, body }) => {
  const response = await server.inject({
    method, url: path, query, payload: body as object | undefined,
    headers: { cookie: req.headers.cookie ?? '' }
  })
  return { status: response.statusCode, body: response.body ? response.json() : null }
}
```

- Telemetry: `preload()` starts the OpenTelemetry SDK from the `OTEL_*` variables; AI spans from this
  package join it when `@ai-sdk/otel` is installed.

## Defaults and limits

| Module | Setting | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| mfa | algorithm, digits, period | SHA1, 6, 30 s |
| mfa | secret size | 20 bytes |
| mfa | verification `window` | 1 (about +/- 30 s) |
| mailer | `secure` | `port === 465` |
| storage | `region` | `us-east-1` |
| storage | presigned URL expiry | 86400 s (24 h) |
| transfer | S3 `partSize` | 8 MiB (S3 minimum 5 MiB) |
| transfer | `maxSize` | unlimited |
| transfer | S3 `region`, addressing | `us-east-1`, path style |
| ai | concurrency | openai 5, mistral 10, google 10, anthropic 5, ollama 2, other 2 |
| ai | concurrency queue | 100 waiters per provider |
| ai | `PgVectorStore` | table `embeddings`, distance `cosine`, `k` 5 |

## Not in this package

- No TypeORM or Drizzle integration and no database connection of its own: `PgVectorStore` takes a query
  function. `global.connection` does not exist in `@volcanicminds/backend` 5.
- No HTTP routes: the backend (or the application) mounts the transfer endpoint and the MCP handler.
- No email templates, no SMS sender, no login endpoints.
